Taraba State Governor Agbu Kefas on Tuesday approved full payment of the Consolidated Academic Tools Allowance, Consolidated Non-Teaching Tools Allowance, and Earned Academic Allowances to staff of the state-owned tertiary institutions, including outstanding arrears dating back to January 2026. The governor also appealed to the striking unions to suspend their industrial action and allow academic activities to resume in the affected institutions. The approval followed the recommendations of a committee set up by the state government to examine wage-related concerns and other issues surrounding the allowances. The governor announced the approval while receiving the committee’s report at the TY Danjuma House, in Jalingo, the state capital. He equally directed the Commissioner for Tertiary Education and his counterpart in the Finance Ministry to see to the modalities of the payments. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “I have received the report of the committee, and I want to announce that I have approved the committee’s recommendations, including 100 per cent payment of CATA, CONTTA and EAA allowances of all outstanding arrears from January 2026. “I want to appeal to the unions to reciprocate the government’s intervention by suspending the strike to enable students to return to their classrooms, especially for those of Taraba State University who were writing their final year examinations. “The Commissioner for Tertiary Education and the Commissioner for Finance are hereby directed to work out modalities for the payment. All allowances due to the striking unions would be paid in full,” he directed. The industrial action, which has disrupted teaching, learning and other academic activities in the state-owned tertiary institutions in the past month, has raised concerns among students, parents and other stakeholders over the implications for academic calendars and students’ progression. The governor urged the unions to always embrace dialogue and cooperation in resolving the dispute, stressing the need to restore normal academic activities in the institutions.
